weaknesses.critique: The quarters being compared have different lengths. Evidence E1 and E6 note that 'Each of our quarters, other than the fourth quarter, ends on the Friday closest to the last day of the corresponding quarterly calendar period.' The third quarter of 2026 ended on October 2, 2026, while the third quarter of 2025 ended on September 26, 2025 - a difference of 6 days. While the evidence confirms revenues increased in absolute terms ($13,380M vs $12,455M), the different quarter lengths could affect the comparability of the year-over-year comparison. However, the claim only states revenues 'increased year over year' without specifying on a same-day basis, so the absolute increase still supports the claim as stated.

The evidence does not provide information about whether the revenue increase was organic or driven by acquisitions, currency effects, or other one-time factors. Evidence E5 mentions structural changes including refranchising operations in India (May 2025) and selling finished product operations in Nigeria (October 2025), which could have affected revenue comparisons. However, the claim makes no attribution about the cause of the increase - it simply states that revenues increased, which is factually supported by the evidence.

There is no weakness in the verdict. The evidence clearly and directly supports the claim that net operating revenues increased year over year for the quarter ended October 2, 2026. The $13,380 million in Q3 2026 compared to $12,455 million in Q3 2025 represents an unambiguous increase, regardless of the underlying drivers or calendar differences.
